claims.text: An AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film can be deposited by Co-FCVAD.
Annealing the AlCrTiZrMo film at 800 °C for 1 hour forms a dense ZrTiO4-containing composite oxide layer.
The dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer prevents continued oxidation of the film.
The annealed AlCrTiZrMo film has excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air.
Annealing at 800 °C for 1 hour gives the AlCrTiZrMo film its best reported tribocorrosion resistance among the studied annealing conditions.
The favorable tribocorrosion resistance of the annealed film results from its stable dense microstructure and mechanical properties.
The coating and annealing treatment will increase surface hardness relative to an untreated component.
The coating and annealing treatment will improve tribocorrosion performance relative to an untreated component.
Intrinsic lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening in the AlCrTiZrMo alloy contribute to the improved surface properties.
Synergistic interactions among the multiple principal elements increase hardness and resistance to oxidation and wear.
The HEA microstructure reinforces surface integrity.
Untreated or conventionally treated metallic components have lower hardness and are more vulnerable to oxidation, wear, and high-temperature corrosive degradation than the proposed coating.
The treatment should remain effective near 800 °C in oxidizing environments.
The treatment should remain effective under combined high-temperature and friction-corrosion service conditions.
The improved surface properties will extend component service life in aggressive environments.
Performance may vary with service temperature, environmental chemistry, film composition, deposition parameters, and annealing conditions.
A same-substrate comparison between coated-and-annealed specimens and untreated controls can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement, exemplified as less than 10%, in hardness, wear resistance, or oxide-layer integrity would falsify the hypothesis.
